steps.what: Monitor investigations of suspected offenders for required fields.
Flag blank warrant, date or notice fields.
Judge whether the investigation met constitutional requirements.
Record whether it was conducted in accordance with those requirements.
Ensure the investigator corrects the failed point.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} file can flag a blank warrant, date or notice field. It does not decide that the investigation met constitutional requirements. The inspector reads the file, records the monitor note, and tells the investigator what to correct. Native required fields are tested before custom code.
tasks.previous_blocker: The check was a reread of the whole file, so a blank warrant line was easy to miss and a present line was easy to treat as lawful.
tasks.enabler_now: A blank field can be flagged. Whether the investigation was lawful still needs the inspector.
tasks.still_hard: Files where the warrant, date or notice is present but the legal test is still unmet.
tasks.human_edge: The inspector knows the difference between a blank field and an investigation that fails the legal test.

ambition.what: The inspector decides on each file whether a missing warrant, date or notice stops the investigation, instead of finding it only at the end.

tasks.altitude: File review stays on the week. A blank-field flag is not a constitutional decision.

reach.task: Check a file for a required field before a decision
reach.learn: Which missing field they treat as a stop and which they still read

evidence.claim: A case screen can flag an empty warrant, date or notice field. It cannot decide that an investigation met a constitutional test.
A blank-field check is not a decision on the lawfulness of an investigation. The inspector makes that decision. The exact national rule on search, notice and time limits is not assumed here.

assumptions: Focal role is the property inspector. Boundary: monitoring one investigation file for warrant, date and notice fields, then a monitor note. The investigation itself is another person's work.

Structured fields are investigation id, warrant id, warrant date and notice date. The investigator produces them. The inspector produces the monitor note. Fallback: a file with no such fields is read in full by the inspector.
Test native required fields in {WORKFLOW} before custom code. The US task is read as a European public authority. The check does not score staff and does not read the narrative.
Upkeep of 2 hours per 100 baseline hours covers the required-field list.
unknowns: The exact national code for search, notice and time limits.
Who may see a file about a suspected offender.
research_questions: What share of files has the fields filled and still fails the legal test?

incremental.description: Keep the warrant, date and notice fields current

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the file has no structured warrant or notice fields, so the inspector reads it as today. High: blank fields are flagged and the inspector still judges the legal test and speaks to the investigator. The judgement is not the flag.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still sites, products, hearings and files. The inspector can stop a report, a disclosure or a sample submission that is not tied to a note they accepted.
reach: Environmental compliance inspectors: which site measurement they will not take from a photograph
Regulatory affairs specialists: which missing field stops a file
Claims adjusters, examiners, and investigators: how a finding stays tied to a note
skills_to_grow: Refusing a draft sentence that has no source note
Reading a checklist without treating it as a permit decision
Keeping a disclosure inside facts already accepted
role.ambitious_version: Every finding the inspector signs can be traced to a note they accepted, and no permit is granted by a checklist.
